Knot reference

Each knot below is listed with what it is for, how well it holds under load compared with the rope alone, and whether it can be untied after it has been loaded. Strength figures are rough and vary with the rope.

KnotUsed forStrength keptUnties after load
BowlineA fixed loop at the end of a line60 to 75 percentEasily
Clove hitchTying a line to a post or rail60 to 65 percentEasily
Figure eight loopA strong loop for climbing harnesses75 to 80 percentWith effort
Sheet bendJoining two ropes of different sizes50 to 60 percentEasily
Round turn and two half hitchesMooring a boat to a ring65 to 70 percentEasily
Trucker's hitchPulling a load tight on a roof rackVariesEasily
Double fisherman'sJoining two ropes for good65 to 70 percentHard
PrusikA friction grip that slides when unloadedVariesEasily
Reef knotTying off a bandage or a sail reef45 percentEasily
Stopper knotKeeping a rope from running through a deviceNot for loadsWith effort
Timber hitchDragging a log or starting a lashingVariesEasily
Alpine butterflyA loop in the middle of a line60 to 65 percentEasily

Never trust a knot you cannot check. Practise each one until you can tie it in the dark, and dress it neatly before it takes a load.
